I found the exact coupling point. I’m removing the `Simulator.resetStatisticsView` flag and making `StatisticsView` reset itself whenever it observes the simulation step move backward, which is the real event it cares about.

item.text:
Removed the remaining UI coupling between the simulation core and the statistics window. [StatisticsView.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R003_module_java/StatisticsView.java:49) now tracks the last recorded simulation step and resets itself when it detects the simulation has restarted, rather than depending on an external `Simulator.resetStatisticsView` flag. That logic is centered in [updatePopulationLineChart()](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R003_module_java/StatisticsView.java:114) and [hasSimulationReset()](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R003_module_java/StatisticsView.java:171).

With that in place, [Simulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R003_module_java/Simulator.java:98) no longer needs to expose or maintain a statistics-reset flag at all, so the reset path is simpler and the statistics view is responsible for its own lifecycle. I also dropped an unused JavaFX import from `StatisticsView` as part of the cleanup.
